question: Can a sparse attention mechanism with linear cost in sequence length keep the empirical benefits and the theoretical expressivity of full quadratic attention, and so allow longer contexts?
hypothesis: Sparse attention built from global, local-window and random connections (a small-world-style graph) with O(1) global tokens preserves full-attention expressivity and improves tasks that need long context.
contributions: BigBird satisfies the known theoretical properties of the full transformer: universal approximator and Turing complete, with O(n) inner products using extra global tokens.
Empirically, longer context helps NLP tasks; state of the art on QA and summarization on several datasets.
A novel application to genomics: long-context MLM pretraining on DNA improves promoter-region and chromatin-profile prediction.

method.summary: BigBird replaces full attention with a sparse pattern of g global tokens, a sliding window of w tokens and r random keys per query, computed blockwise so that it runs as dense tensor ops on GPU/TPU. Models are warm-started from RoBERTa (or Pegasus for large summarization), pretrained with MLM at 4096 tokens, then fine-tuned on QA, classification, summarization and DNA tasks.
method.task: Long-context encoder pretraining (MLM) and fine-tuning for QA, document classification, summarization, DNA modelling

models.name: BigBird-ITC base
models.architecture: BERT/RoBERTa-style encoder with block sparse attention, some existing tokens made global

models.name: BigBird-ETC base
models.architecture: as ITC but extra global tokens added, relative position encoding

other.block_length: almost doubled to 169 for ETC; ITC kept at base size

models.name: BigBird-RoBERTa
models.init_from: BigBird MLM base model (from RoBERTa); encoder-decoder weights shared except encoder-decoder attention

training.objective: MLM (15% masking) for pretraining; cross-entropy fine-tuning for QA/classification; teacher-forced cross-entropy for summarization; MLM+NSP for DNA pretraining; BCE for DNA tasks
training.optimizer: Adam (base MLM, QA, classification, DNA); LAMB for large WikiHop; Adafactor for BigBird-Pegasus
training.lr: 1e-4 base MLM (Table 8); QA base-size see Table 12; large QA 3e-5 (HotpotQA) and {5,10}e-5 / {3,5}e-5 / {2,5}e-5 for others (Table 13); classification 5e-6 to 5e-5 (Table 14); summarization 1e-5 (base), 1e-4 (large)
training.lr_schedule: linear decay (MLM, DNA, classification); square-root decay (summarization)
training.warmup: 10,000 steps (MLM, summarization, DNA); first 10% of steps (classification)
training.batch_size: 256 base MLM; 2048 large MLM; QA 32-128; classification 32-64; summarization 128; DNA 256
training.steps: DNA pretraining 1000000; promoter 711; chromatin 500000; NLP MLM steps not stated
training.epochs: large QA: HotpotQA {5,9}, NaturalQ {3,5}, TriviaQA {3,5}, WikiHop {5,10}; classification IMDb 40, Arxiv 10, Patents 3, Hyperpartisan 15, Yelp-5 2
training.regularisation: variant of contrastive predictive coding (dual encoder) for QA; position embedding for ITC, relative position encoding for ETC
training.hardware: TPUv3: 8x8 for MLM and DNA; 4x2 to 4x8 for QA, classification, summarization; DNA fine-tuning 8x8
training.compute: 8 x 8 TPUv3 chips for pretraining; trained on 16GB memory per chip with batch 32-64
training.seeds: IMDb and Hyperpartisan repeated 5 times; others not stated

inference.retrieval: QA evidence retrieved with crude systems like TF-IDF/BM25 (as in the datasets)

metrics.definition: F1 for HotpotQA, NQ, TriviaQA; accuracy for WikiHop

There is no free lunch: finding furthest vectors needs one layer with full attention but near-linear layers with any sparse attention of O~(n) edges.
results.setup: theoretical, under the Orthogonal Vectors Conjecture

limits: Sparse attention is provably weaker for some tasks: under the Orthogonal Vectors Conjecture, the furthest-vector task needs ~n layers for any sparse attention with ~n edges (Sec 3.4).
The 8x longer sequence claim is stated without a memory or speed measurement; training is on 16GB chips at batch 32-64.
Sparse attention only on the encoder; decoder keeps full attention because outputs are short.
Large QA test model uses window 507 and no random tokens, so the headline QA results come from ETC without random attention; random attention only used in ITC.
Promoter F1 is inflated by overlap between negative-example construction and MLM pretraining (App F.2).
No latency, throughput or kernel benchmark; efficiency is argued by complexity and blockification, not measured.
Encoder-only/bidirectional; autoregressive decoding with KV cache is not evaluated.

code.snippet: ATTN_D(X)_i = x_i + sum_h sigma( Q_h(x_i) K_h(X_N(i))^T ) . V_h(X_N(i))
